title: Greedy largest-empty-circle initialisation
spec: For fresh starts (no crossover), build the initial centres one at a time. Sample 2000 candidate points uniformly in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 with rng, and place the next centre at the candidate whose distance to the nearest existing centre (and to the walls) is largest. Initial radii are INIT_RADIUS for all circles. Keep the rest of the loop unchanged. The rest of the pipeline (SLSQP, repair, pool) stays as in slot 11.

title: Overcomplete start, drop the smallest circles
spec: For fresh starts, solve the SLSQP problem with n+k circles (k=2) instead of n, using random centres and INIT_RADIUS radii. After the solve, sort by radius and delete the k smallest circles, then clip, repair and score the remaining n circles as usual. The extra circles give the optimiser room to rearrange, and the discard step keeps the output at exactly n circles. Keep the pool logic unchanged.

title: Coordinate-wise greedy radius growth polish
spec: After repair, polish each packing with a cheap greedy growth pass. Visit circles in a random order drawn from rng. For each circle, set its radius to the largest value allowed by the walls and by the current radii of its neighbours (min over j of dist(i,j)-r_j, and walls). Repeat the sweep 5 times, stopping early if the sum stops changing by more than 1e-12. Apply this to the final best packing and to each pool member before it is stored. Use exact double-precision arithmetic and keep SHRINK at 1e-9 so the harness check still passes.

title: Dihedral transform of pool members before crossover
spec: In _cross, before cutting, apply a random element of the dihedral group of the square to each of the two parent packings (a random choice among the 8 symmetries: swap x and y, and/or flip x and/or flip y, mapping centres into [0,1]^2 and keeping radii). This lets the vertical cut combine different orientations of good packings. Everything else (cut position, filling, pool update) stays as before.

title: Random cut axis in crossover
spec: Currently _cross always cuts vertically at x=t. Choose the cut axis at random per crossover: with probability 0.5 use x as now, otherwise use y (keep circles with centre y below t from parent a and y at or above t from parent b). Draw t uniformly from [0.3, 0.7] as before. Filling of missing circles and trimming of surplus circles stay unchanged.

title: Metropolis acceptance into the elite pool
spec: Replace the strict elitist pool update with a Metropolis rule. A new packing with radius sum S_new enters the pool if it is among the top 5 or, with probability exp((S_new - S_worst)/T), replaces the worst member, where S_worst is the smallest sum in the pool and T is 0.005 times the sum of the best member. Keep the best packing returned separately so the final answer is always the best ever found. Use rng for the acceptance draw.

title: Single-circle Metropolis moves on the best packing
spec: After the restart loop has used the first 60% of the time budget, run a simulated-annealing phase on the best packing. Each move picks one random circle, moves its centre by a Gaussian step with sd 0.05 (clipped into the box), and recomputes all radii with the greedy clearance rule (each radius is the largest value satisfying walls and neighbours, given the other radii held fixed in a sweep). Accept the move with the Metropolis rule at temperature decreasing linearly from 0.002 to 0. Keep the best state seen. Run this until the time budget is used. The pool and SLSQP restarts still run for the first part of the time.

title: Loose tolerance for fresh starts, tight tolerance for pool polish
spec: Pass ftol to the SLSQP call. For fresh random starts use ftol=1e-5 so each run stops early and more restarts fit into the budget. For restarts seeded from the pool (crossover and perturbation), use ftol=1e-10 and the existing MAX_ITER. Keep the existing constraint set and repair. This only changes the stopping rule of the solver, not the formulation.

title: Centre-based diversity filter for the pool
spec: Replace the sorted-radius diversity test with a centre-based test. Before adding a new packing to the pool, compute for each existing member the mean over circles of the distance from each centre to its nearest centre in the other packing. If the minimum of this value over the pool is below 0.02, the new packing is a near duplicate: keep only the one with the larger radius sum. Otherwise insert it and keep the top 8 by radius sum. Everything else (crossover, perturbation, time loop) stays as in the incumbent.

title: Scrambled van der Corput centres for fresh starts
spec: For fresh random starts, draw the initial centres from a low-discrepancy set instead of uniform random. Build a 2D Halton point set with bases 2 and 3 of size n, shifted by a random offset drawn from rng (with modulo 1 wrap-around), and map it into [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2. Use these centres and INIT_RADIUS radii as the SLSQP start. Keep the crossover and pool logic unchanged, so only the fresh-start distribution differs.

title: Penalty relaxation on fresh starts plus pool of 12
spec: Adopt slot 11 as base: for fresh random starts, relax centres with L-BFGS-B on a smooth overlap/wall penalty energy with target radii about 0.09 before SLSQP. Also use a pool of 12 with a diversity filter that skips packings whose sorted radius vector is within 1e-3 L2 of a pool member. Crossover and jitter restarts draw from this pool. Keep everything else unchanged.

title: Penalty relaxation with randomised target radius
spec: In the penalty-energy relaxation of fresh starts, draw a per-start target radius uniformly from [0.07, 0.11] for all circles. Then start SLSQP with radii set to 0.8 times the target. This diversifies the basins reached by fresh starts. Keep pool of 5 and the rest as in slot 11.

title: Size-mixed relaxation targets
spec: In the penalty relaxation of fresh starts, give each circle its own target radius from a mixture: 8 circles at about 0.13, the other 24 at about 0.075, with the large circles chosen at random. Relax the centres by L-BFGS-B against the sum of squared overlaps of the target radii, then run SLSQP with these target radii as the initial radii. Compare with equal targets.

title: Annealed inflating penalty relaxation
spec: Replace the single penalty relaxation of fresh starts with 3 successive L-BFGS-B stages (30 iterations each), where target radius grows 0.06, 0.08, 0.095 with warm-started centres. Then run SLSQP with radii set to 0.9 times the final target. This gives a gentle compression that avoids jamming early.

title: Batch screening of relaxed starts by penalty energy
spec: Per restart, generate 8 random starts, relax each with a short penalty L-BFGS-B (target radius 0.09), and send only the one with lowest final penalty energy to SLSQP. The relaxation is cheap compared with SLSQP, so SLSQP is spent on the most promising starts. Keep the pool of 5 and crossover as is.

title: Relocation moves on pool members
spec: Replace the crossover restarts (70 percent of the time) with a relocation move. Pick a pool member, pick one circle with probability proportional to 1/radius, and move it to a random location. Set its radius to 0.03, then run SLSQP. Combine with penalty-relaxed fresh starts and a pool of 12 with the 1e-3 diversity filter.

title: Swap-radius moves between neighbouring circles
spec: Add a restart type with probability 0.3. Take a random pool member, pick two circles with different radii that are neighbours (centre distance below 1.2 times the sum of their radii), and swap their centres. Keep the radii as they are, shrink all radii by 10 percent and run SLSQP. This tests exchanges of big and small circles without large perturbation. Use it alongside the slot 11 relaxation.

title: Noisy lattice starts with penalty relaxation, pool 12
spec: Fresh starts: 50 percent a noisy staggered lattice (row counts random in 5 to 7, noise sd 0.02), 50 percent uniform random. All are relaxed by penalty L-BFGS-B. Use pool 12 with the 1e-3 sorted-radius filter and 70 percent crossover from the pool. This combines slots 32 and 18 for a replicated run.

title: Smaller MAX_ITER for relaxed starts with adaptive extension
spec: Since penalty-relaxed starts begin near feasible, run SLSQP with MAX_ITER 100 first. If the resulting radius sum is within 0.01 of the best in the pool, continue with SLSQP warm-started for 200 more iterations. This frees time for more restarts. Use slot 11 relaxation for fresh starts.

title: Final exact feasibility polish with tighter shrink
spec: Keep the slot 11 setup. Change SHRINK from 1e-9 to 1e-12, and make _repair run a second pass that verifies exactly in double precision that every pair distance minus the radii sum is at least 1e-11 and every wall gap is at least 1e-11. If a pair violates this, shrink its two radii by the overlap. This recovers about 1e-8 per circle with no validity risk.

title: Best-radius-profile restarts with penalty relaxation
spec: For 40% of the fresh starts (once the pool is non-empty), take the sorted radius vector of the best pool packing and multiply it by 0.97. Randomly permute these radii over n uniform random centres in [0.1, 0.9]^2. Relax only the centres with scipy L-BFGS-B (maxiter 150) on E = sum over pairs max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)^2 + sum over circles of max(0, r_i - x_i)^2 + max(0, r_i - y_i)^2 + max(0, x_i + r_i - 1)^2 + max(0, y_i + r_i - 1)^2, using the analytic gradient and bounds [0, 1] on the coordinates. Pass the relaxed centres and these radii as x0 to _solve_once. Other starts stay as they are now. Use the solve rng for all randomness.

title: Greedy largest-hole sequential insertion starts
spec: Replace half of the fresh random x0 with a greedy start. Place the first centre uniformly at random. For each next circle, sample 400 random candidate points and pick the one that maximises min(distance to the nearest placed centre minus that centre's provisional radius, distance to the nearest wall). Set its provisional radius to 0.9 times that clearance, capped at 0.15. Use the centres and provisional radii (floored at 0.01) as x0 for _solve_once. Use the solve rng only.

title: Symmetry-transformed parents in crossover
spec: In _cross, before the cut, apply an independently chosen random symmetry of the square to each parent. There are 8 (identity, rotations by 90/180/270 degrees, reflections in x=0.5, y=0.5 and both diagonals), implemented as coordinate maps on the centres; radii are unchanged. This lets the left part of one optimum combine with differently oriented parts of another. Leave everything else in _cross and solve unchanged.

title: Random-angle median cut crossover
spec: Change _cross so that it cuts along a line in a random direction instead of the x-threshold. Draw an angle theta uniformly in [0, pi) and a unit vector u = (cos theta, sin theta). Project the centres of both parents onto u. Pick k = rng.integers(10, n-9). Take the k circles of parent A with the smallest projections, then fill with the circles of parent B, in increasing projection order, whose projection exceeds the k-th projection of A, until there are n circles. If B runs out, add random circles of radius INIT_RADIUS. The child always has exactly n circles, so no random dropping is needed.

title: Rattler relocation by contact count
spec: For 30% of the restarts once the pool has at least 1 member, pick a random pool packing and count each circle's contacts: neighbours or walls with gap < 1e-6. Choose one random circle among those with at most 2 contacts. If there is none, choose the smallest circle. Move its centre to the best of 500 random points, the one with the largest clearance to all other circles and the walls. Set its radius to 0.5 times that clearance, and use the result as x0 for _solve_once. This replaces some crossover starts, and the pool logic is unchanged.

title: Three independent sub-run portfolio
spec: Split the restart loop into 3 equal time slices of TIME_FRACTION*time_limit/3. Each slice has its own empty pool of 5, so crossover only mixes packings found in that slice. Keep a global best across slices and return it. The aim is to avoid early pool collapse onto one basin. No other changes.

title: Scrambled Sobol fresh centres
spec: Replace uniform random fresh centres in _solve_once with scrambled Sobol points. Use scipy.stats.qmc.Sobol(d=2, scramble=True, seed=int(rng.integers(2**31))).random(32)[:n], mapped affinely into [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 and then given Gaussian jitter of sd 0.01. Radii stay at INIT_RADIUS. The more even spread should start SLSQP with fewer badly overlapping circles. The crossover and pool are unchanged.

title: Radius swap moves between unequal neighbours
spec: For 25% of restarts once the pool is non-empty, take the best pool packing and pick a random pair of touching circles (gap < 1e-4) whose radii differ by at least 20%. Swap their radii and then shrink both to 0.9 times their new values so that the start is closer to feasible. Use the resulting (centres, radii) as x0 for _solve_once. Do not jitter anything else. This is a minimal topology change in the size arrangement, distinct from jitter or relocation.

title: Pool replacement by nearest neighbour (crowding)
spec: Change the pool update from keep-top-5 to deterministic crowding with a pool of 8. A new packing whose sum is better than the worst pool member replaces the pool member with the closest sorted radius vector (L2), but only if the new packing is better than that member. Otherwise it replaces the worst member, but only when the closest L2 distance exceeds 1e-3. This keeps several distinct basins alive for crossover. The best is tracked separately as now.

title: Remove radius-nonnegativity constraints and use bounds
spec: In _solve_once, drop the final r block from the constraint vector in cons. Instead pass SLSQP bounds: centres in [0, 1] and radii in [0, 0.5]. This removes n inequality constraints and keeps the variables in the box during iterations, which should give fewer iterations per solve and more restarts. Keep the remaining constraints and the rest of the code unchanged. _repair still guarantees validity.

title: Penalty-relaxed fresh starts plus relocation moves
spec: Two changes to how SLSQP start points are made. (a) Fresh starts: draw centres uniformly in [0.1, 0.9]^2, then relax the centres only with scipy L-BFGS-B (maxiter 60, bounds [R, 1-R]) on the energy E = sum over pairs of max(0, 2R - d_ij)^2 with a fixed target radius R = 0.09, using an analytic gradient. Pass the relaxed centres with radii 0.05 to SLSQP. (b) Replace _cross by a relocation move: copy a random pool member, pick one circle with probability proportional to 1/radius, move its centre to the point of largest clearance among 400 uniformly sampled candidate points (clearance = min of wall distance and distance to the other centres minus their radii), set its radius to max(0.01, 0.9 * clearance), and use that as x0. Keep the 70% pool-move / 30% fresh split, the pool of 5, the repair step and the time loop unchanged.

title: Symmetry-aligned crossover with random cut axis
spec: Change _cross only. Before combining the two parents, apply one of the 8 symmetries of the square (identity, 3 rotations about (0.5, 0.5), 4 reflections) chosen uniformly at random to parent b's centres, and with probability 0.5 swap the x and y columns of both parents so that the cut is horizontal instead of vertical. Then do the existing cut at t in [0.3, 0.7], including the existing trimming or random filling to n circles. This lets the crossover combine a good left half of one packing with a good top, bottom or mirrored half of another instead of only matching x-ranges. Everything else stays the same.

title: Fresh starts with radii copied from the best packing
spec: Once the pool is non-empty, build fresh starts (the 30% non-crossover branch) from the size distribution of the best pool member instead of equal radii 0.05: take its radius vector, multiply by 0.85, sort descending, and place the circles one at a time, largest first, at a uniformly sampled centre that does not overlap already placed circles and stays inside the walls (up to 200 tries per circle; on failure keep the last sample). Pass these centres and radii to SLSQP as x0. Before the pool has a member, keep the current uniform start. The aim is to explore new arrangements while keeping a size mix known to score well.

title: Greedy max-clearance constructive starts
spec: Replace uniform random fresh starts by a greedy construction. Sample 600 candidate points uniformly in the unit square once per start. Draw a radius cap for this start uniformly in [0.08, 0.13]. Then n times: for every candidate compute its clearance = min(distance to the 4 walls, distance to each placed centre minus that circle's radius); among the 10 candidates with the largest clearance pick one at random using the seeded rng; place a circle there with radius min(cap, clearance) * 0.9. If the clearance is not positive, place radius 0.005 at a random point. Use these centres and radii as x0 for SLSQP. Crossover starts, the pool, the repair step and the time loop stay the same.

title: Hole-filling for missing circles in crossover
spec: In _cross, when the child has fewer than n circles, do not add circles at uniformly random positions with radius 0.05. Instead add them one at a time at the point of largest clearance among 500 uniformly sampled candidate points, where clearance = min(distance to walls, distance to each existing child centre minus its radius), with radius max(0.01, 0.9 * clearance). When the child has more than n circles, do not delete at random: repeatedly delete the circle with the largest total overlap with the others (sum of max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)), breaking ties by the smallest radius. The rest of the script is unchanged.

title: Crowding replacement in the pool
spec: Change how the pool is updated in solve; the pool size stays 5. Define the distance between two packings as the L2 norm of the difference of their descending-sorted radius vectors. When a new packing arrives and the pool is full: find the pool member closest to it; if that distance is below 0.02, the new packing replaces that member only if its radius sum is larger (otherwise it is dropped); if no member is that close, it replaces the worst member if its radius sum is larger than the worst. This keeps the pool from filling with copies of one basin, so crossover mixes really different packings. The best-so-far tracking and everything else stay the same.

title: Stagnation-triggered pool reset
spec: Count consecutive restarts that did not improve the best radius sum by more than 1e-7. When the count reaches 12, empty the pool (the global best is kept separately in `best` and is still returned at the end), reset the counter, and let the search rebuild a new pool from fresh random starts and their crossovers. Do not do a reset when less than 25% of the search time is left. No other change. The aim is to stop a seed that has converged to a second-rate basin from spending the rest of its time on children of that basin.

title: Three islands, then a merged final phase
spec: Split the search time (TIME_FRACTION * time_limit) into four equal phases. In phases 1 to 3 run the existing loop (fresh starts, 70% crossover once the pool has 2, pool of 5) with a separate, initially empty pool per phase, all drawing from the same seeded rng. In phase 4 form a merged pool from the best 2 packings of each island (6 members, keep pool size 6) and run the same loop with crossover probability 0.9. Return the best packing seen in any phase. This gives three independent populations per seed and then recombines their best, to reduce the seed-to-seed spread.

title: Band-slide mutation of pool members
spec: Add a third kind of start, used for 30% of restarts once the pool has 2 members (then 50% crossover, 20% fresh). Take a random pool member, choose an axis (x or y) at random and a band [a, a + w] on the other coordinate with w uniform in [0.2, 0.4] and a uniform in [0, 1 - w]. Shift every circle whose centre lies in the band by the same offset delta along the chosen axis, delta uniform in [-0.08, 0.08], clip the centres to [r, 1 - r], multiply all radii by 0.95, and run SLSQP from that point. Sliding a whole row against its neighbours changes the stacking between rows, a structured move that jitter and single-circle moves cannot make.

title: Over-seed with n+2 circles, then drop the two smallest
spec: For fresh starts only (not crossover children): run _solve_once on n + 2 circles with maxiter 80 (make the circle count and maxiter arguments of _solve_once, uniform random start as now). Then delete the 2 circles with the smallest radii from the result and run SLSQP again on the remaining n circles from that point with MAX_ITER iterations. The repair step, the pool and the time loop work on the n-circle result as before. The extra circles let the solver decide which positions are useless before they are removed, which should give better n-circle arrangements than starting with exactly n. Check that one fresh start still finishes well within the time budget so that the 45 s limit is never reached.
